name: DataGridView
purpose: A DataGridView displays and edits tabular data in rows and columns. It can show a list of objects, a DataTable or rows you add manually.
whenToUse: Show records with several fields, such as customers or orders.
Let users edit, sort, add and delete rows.
Bind to a list, DataTable or BindingSource.
realWorldExamples: A customer list with Name, City and Phone columns.
An invoice screen with an editable list of line items.
A results grid that shows the rows of a SQL query.
defaultAppearance: A grid with a header row showing column names, a row-header column on the left, thin cell borders, and alternating selection highlight. An empty 'new row' appears at the bottom when AllowUserToAddRows is true.

commonMistakes.mistake: Binding a plain List<T> and seeing no updates after adding items.
commonMistakes.fix: Bind a BindingList<T> or wrap the list in a BindingSource so the grid is notified of changes.

commonMistakes.mistake: Loading thousands of rows by adding them one at a time.
commonMistakes.fix: Bind the data source once, or use VirtualMode for very large data sets.

commonMistakes.mistake: Reading CurrentRow when no row is selected, which throws NullReferenceException.
commonMistakes.fix: Check for null, and check SelectedRows.Count, before using it.

relatedNotes.name: ListBox
relatedNotes.difference: A simple one-column list; use DataGridView when items have several fields.

relatedNotes.name: BindingSource
relatedNotes.difference: Sits between the data and the grid, adding sorting, filtering and current-record tracking.

relatedNotes.name: BindingNavigator
relatedNotes.difference: A toolbar to move through and add or delete records in the bound data.

name: BindingSource
purpose: A BindingSource is a non-visual component that sits between a data source and bound controls. It manages the current record, sorting, filtering and change notification.
whenToUse: Bind several controls to the same list so they stay in sync.
Sort or filter data without changing the underlying collection.
Move through records with Position or a BindingNavigator.
realWorldExamples: A master/detail screen where choosing a customer shows their orders.
A form that binds TextBoxes to the current record of a list.
A grid whose rows can be filtered by a search box.
defaultAppearance: BindingSource has no appearance; it appears in the component tray under the form designer. It shows nothing at run time, and the controls bound to it display the data.

commonMistakes.mistake: Setting DataSource to a type that is not a list and expecting rows.
commonMistakes.fix: Bind to a list or collection (or a single object for one record) and set DataMember for sub-lists.

commonMistakes.mistake: Using Filter with a data source that does not support it.
commonMistakes.fix: Filter and Sort work with sources such as DataView or a BindingList that implements IBindingListView; otherwise filter in code.

commonMistakes.mistake: Not calling EndEdit before saving, which loses the last typed value.
commonMistakes.fix: Call EndEdit() on the BindingSource before reading or saving the data.

relatedNotes.name: DataGridView
relatedNotes.difference: The visible grid that is commonly bound to a BindingSource.

relatedNotes.name: BindingNavigator
relatedNotes.difference: The toolbar that moves the BindingSource's current position.

relatedNotes.name: ComboBox
relatedNotes.difference: A control that can be bound to a BindingSource through DataSource, DisplayMember and ValueMember.

name: BindingNavigator
purpose: A BindingNavigator is a toolbar with buttons to move to the first, previous, next and last record of a BindingSource, and to add or delete records.
whenToUse: Browse records one at a time in a detail form.
Provide add and delete buttons for bound data.
Show 'record N of M' without writing navigation code.
realWorldExamples: A customer detail form with record navigation at the top.
A simple data entry form for a table of products.
A tool for reviewing a list of items one by one.
defaultAppearance: A ToolStrip docked at the top of the form with buttons for Move first, Previous, a position box ('1' of 5), Next, Last, Add new and Delete.

commonMistakes.mistake: Adding a navigator and finding that it does nothing.
commonMistakes.fix: Set its BindingSource property to the BindingSource that holds the data.
The navigator only moves and edits the in-memory list; add your own Save button that writes to the database or file.

commonMistakes.mistake: Removing a button and breaking the navigator.
commonMistakes.fix: Set the item's Visible or Enabled property, or replace the item and assign it to the matching property such as DeleteItem.

relatedNotes.name: BindingSource
relatedNotes.difference: Provides the data and the current position that the navigator controls.

relatedNotes.name: DataGridView
relatedNotes.difference: Shows many records at once; a navigator is for moving between records.

relatedNotes.name: ToolStrip
relatedNotes.difference: The base class that BindingNavigator extends with data buttons.
